summary: NASA has scheduled coverage for the upcoming launch and arrival of SpaceX’s 35th commercial resupply mission to the International Space Station, alongside the scheduled departure of Northrop Grumman’s CRS-24 cargo craft. In defense and policy developments, the European Union strengthened collective space security through a mutual defense pact, while the U.S. Space Force is advancing a new GPS ground plan following the cancellation of the OCX program. On the commercial front, Xona has increased production ahead of its Pulsar satellite launch, HawkEye 360 expanded its radio-frequency tracking to orbital targets, and ArbaLabs deployed an artificial intelligence verification demonstration on South Korea’s Nuri rocket. Planetary and space science achievements include NASA’s Curiosity rover reaching a major elevation milestone on Mars and capturing photos of a Martian dawn, alongside new research demonstrating that simulated lunar soil combined with recyclable thermoplastics could support off-world manufacturing. In astronomy, scientists identified exotic methanol in planet-forming regions, a record-breaking gamma-ray burst engine that remained active for nearly a month, and a 12.5-billion-year-old radio galaxy that may be the most powerful ever detected. Looking ahead, space enthusiasts should watch for NASA’s upcoming live broadcast and launch operations for the SpaceX 35th commercial resupply mission to the space station.
